title: The Morning a Governor Told James Mwangi to Write His Resignation
conflicts: Year: slate said 1994; Mwangi's own account (Business Daily 2024) puts the governor meeting in early 1993, Roland Berger dates his move to 1994, and Stanford/MicroSave give 1995 for his formal appointment as finance director. The story follows Mwangi for the meeting and uses 1995 for the appointment. Pay cut: Sh360,000 to Sh60,000 a month (Business Daily, about 83%) against 94% (Roland Berger); both given with attribution. Accumulated losses: KSh 33m (MicroSave, Stanford) against Sh35m (Business Daily); the story says 'more than Sh30 million'. Accounts: nearly 3,000 (Roland Berger) against about 12,000 deposit clients in 1994 (MicroSave chart); left out. Bank conversion: 2007 (Roland Berger) against end of 2004 (MicroSave, Business Daily); 2004 used.
notes: approx_date set to 1993, not the slate's 1994. The quote challenges the decision: Saadi's advice to an accountant with a family who seeks a risky royal post.
